requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
**Verdict: false.** The selector logic is largely implemented and tested, but one part of it has no `{impl}` marker for this requirement.

**What is covered**
- **Grammar and parsing.** `parse_selector`, `split_segments` and `parse_segment` in `src/outline/selector.rs` handle:
  - the empty selector, which selects the root;
  - `kind[name]` and `kind@<12 hex>` segments;
  - the `#N` suffix;
  - rejection of malformed selectors.
- **Encoding.** `encode_name` and `decode_name` percent-encode `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and whitespace as UTF-8 bytes, and they reverse each other.
- **Anonymous labels.** `Builder::finish` in `src/outline/mod.rs` builds the label from `identity_hash[..HASH_DIGITS]` with `HASH_DIGITS` = 12.
- **Disambiguation.** `disambiguate` appends one-based `#N` in source order to sibling segments that would otherwise be identical, and skips `line` nodes. `Outline::resolve` resolves a `line` segment to the first line with that content.
- **No line numbers.** No selector contains a line number.
- **Resolution errors.** `ParsedSource::resolve` in `src/inputs.rs` reports invalid, ambiguous and missing selectors.
- **Tests.**
  - `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` and `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` in `src/outline/selector.rs`.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`, `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` and `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` in `src/outline/tests.rs`.
  
  Together they cover the empty selector, ambiguous and missing selectors, `#N` ordinals, hash stability under insertion and edits, interchangeable lines, and an encoded name (`impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`).

**Gap: incomplete `{impl}` marking**
- `plain_text` in `src/outline/mod.rs` (lines 235–280) builds the `line@<12-hex>` segment for every line node. It does so with `Segment::base("line", &Label::Hash(hash[..HASH_DIGITS]))`, and it sets each node's `selector` and `segment`. This is the anonymous-segment obligation, and it is also what makes line selectors a bare `line@hash` that is never `#N`-suffixed. The function is marked `{impl}` only for `outlines` and `structural_hash`, not for `outline_selectors`.
- `root_node` (lines 282–304) sets the root's empty `segment` and `selector`. This is the "empty selector selects the root" convention, and it is marked `{impl}` only for `outlines`.

The task says code that implements part of the requirement without an `{impl}` reference to it is a gap. No FIXME in the sources acknowledges this, so the result is false rather than FIXME. Adding `{impl}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`` to `plain_text` and `root_node` would close it.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile
MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text MUST be hashed,
not its delimiter tokens such as `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`,
so reflowing it across more or fewer lines does not change the hash. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
